newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC pilot week sees small volume traded.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC pilot week sees small volume traded.

text.p: Romania's nascent over-the-counter (OTC) market system said on Friday it had ended a pilot one-week stage of trading.
Market players were undeterred by the tiny volumes traded. Only around 3,000 shares, a turnover of 8.9 million lei, changed hands.
"Turnover is puny, it's less than the stock exchange makes on a bad day, but still, it's a start," a broker said.
The pilot phase on the RASDAQ system started on October 25 and involved seven stocks, a system statement said.

The RASDAQ, modelled on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange under a capital market project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development, opened officially at end-September and went through testing till last Friday.

The statement said only three stocks -- Bijuteria SA jewellery making and marketing company, Turbomecanica SA plane engine maker and Constructii Feroviare Moldova railway construction company -- had trades during the week.
The OTC market is expected to hold daily sessions from Monday to Friday next week.
Brokers see the new system as bound to gain in strength, becoming a welcome rival to the bourse.
"Volumes will eventually rise on the OTC and the bourse itself will have to work to boost trading on its floor," said an exchange trader.

Romania's stock exchange, which trades only 13 stocks, has seen only lacklustre activity in recent months. It expects to fare better when 21 companies which have already applied for listing begin trading.

The RASDAQ is expected to eventually trade shares in some 5,000 medium-sized companies, most of them privatised under the country's mass selloff programme. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
